summary: Customer payment failures are caused by the expiry at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z of payment-service's mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) to the external bank-partner-api, with no automated renewal (cert-watcher warned at 10:20 and 11:50). From 12:15:27 mTLS handshakes were rejected (TLS alert 45), payments were marked PENDING_RETRY, bank_api_error_rate hit 100% and payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5%. The HTTP error_rate panel stayed green (~0.2%) because failed transfers are async/retryable and not surfaced as 5xx, which is why the dashboard was misleading. Root-cause category: credential_expiry, originating in payment-service. All alternatives (partner outage, timeout config change, deploy, resource exhaustion) are contradicted by evidence.", "facts": ["payment-service's bank client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal had notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (F1)", "mTLS handshakes with bank-partner-api were rejected as 'expired certificate (alert 45)' from 12:16:44 (F2, F3)", "bank_api_error_rate rose from 0.2% to 100% at the 12:16 bucket (F4)", "payment_success_rate fell from 99.45% to ~2.55% at 12:16 (F5)", "HTTP error_rate stayed flat ~0.2% throughout, i.e., the dashboard was a false green (F6)", "request_rate steady, CPU ~30% flat, restarts 0 -> not a resource/capacity fault (F7)", "Only change was cfg-2502 timeout 3000->5000 at 11:20; only deploy dep-5510 settlement v1.9.0 at 10:30 (F8)", "bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry (F9)", "Historical HIST-106 was an identical mTLS cert expiry with no renewal automation (F10)"]

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired payment-service mTLS client certificate to bank-partner-api
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The payment-service client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z with no automated renewal, so all mTLS handshakes to the external bank-partner-api are rejected (TLS alert 45). Payments are marked PENDING_RETRY and effectively fail, while the HTTP 5xx-based error_rate panel stays flat because these failures are not surfaced as 5xx.

causal_chain.claim: Client cert notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; cert-watcher warned at 10:20 and 11:50 with no renewal
Cert expires -> mTLS handshakes to bank-partner-api rejected (TLS alert 45) starting 12:15:27
payments marked PENDING_RETRY -> payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%, bank_api_error_rate 100%
Failures not returned as HTTP 5xx -> error_rate dashboard stays green (~0.2%)

assumptions: The bank-partner-api itself is healthy and only rejects our expired client cert (vendor has no telemetry).
No server-side cert of the bank is involved; error text explicitly attributes the expiry to 'our client cert'.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank-partner-api (external dependency) outage/degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external bank partner is failing, causing payment failures independent of our certificate.
assumptions: The partner could be rejecting valid certs.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Logs explicitly say the failure is 'our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' expired (alert 45), a client-side credential problem, and the cert-watcher had already flagged the impending expiry; onset coincides exactly with 12:15 expiry.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change (bank API timeout) or unrelated deployment caused failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20 bank.api.timeout_ms increase or the 10:30 settlement-service deploy caused the payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The change was 55 min before onset and raised a timeout (would not cause TLS rejections); failures align to the 12:15 cert expiry, and error messages are TLS certificate errors, not timeouts. settlement-service GC/clock warnings are unrelated.

assumptions: The bank-partner-api is otherwise healthy and is rejecting requests solely due to our expired client certificate.
HTTP error_rate is defined on 5xx responses, so async/retryable payment failures (PENDING_RETRY) do not appear in it.

timeline.event: cert-watcher warns bank client cert expires in 115 min (notAfter 12:15:00)
config change cfg-2502 raises bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 (separate, not the cause)
cert-watcher warns cert expires in 25 min; no renewal occurs
First mTLS handshake rejection; payments marked PENDING_RETRY
Support reports ~40 failed-transfer tickets; HTTP error-rate panel still green

recommended_actions.action: Rotate/renew the payment-service client certificate for bank-partner-api (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) and reload it, then replay the PENDING_RETRY payments
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired client cert is the direct cause; renewing it restores mTLS and clears the PENDING_RETRY backlog.

recommended_actions.action: Add/verify automated certificate renewal (cert-manager/ACME) and a hard expiry alert well before notAfter for payment-service
recommended_actions.rationale: cert-watcher only warned and no renewal happened, matching the prior HIST-106 failure.

recommended_actions.action: Fix monitoring: alert on bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (business metrics), not just the HTTP 5xx error_rate panel
recommended_actions.rationale: The 5xx-based error_rate stayed green while 97% of payments actually failed, hiding the incident.

recommended_actions.action: Add a dead-letter/alerting path for payments stuck in PENDING_RETRY so async failures page on-call
recommended_actions.rationale: Masked failures produced customer tickets before any internal alert.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api has no telemetry, so we cannot independently confirm the partner side is healthy from inside our systems (relied on the explicit 'our client cert ... expired' error text).
No explicit audit log of the certificate renewal process was available to show why renewal did not run before expiry.

findings.statement: payment-service logged a cert-watcher warning that its bank client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal would expire at notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, at 10:20:44 (115 min before) and 11:50:26 (25 min before).

findings.statement: payment-service bank_api_error_rate jumped from 0.2% at 12:00 to 100% from the 12:16 bucket through 13:52.
payment-service payment_success_rate collapsed from 99.45% at 12:00 to ~2.55% at 12:16 and stayed near 2-3% through 13:52.
payment-service HTTP error_rate stayed flat ~0.16-0.26% across the whole 12:00-13:52 window (the 'green' dashboard), contradicting a 5xx-visible failure.
payment-service request_rate stayed steady ~98-102 req/s and latency_p99 actually fell from ~317ms to ~140ms after onset; CPU ~30% flat; restarts all 0.
The only config change in the window was payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00; the only deployment was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00. No rollback recorded.
bank-partner-api is an external vendor dependency with has_telemetry=false; payment-service calls it (kind external).
Historical incident HIST-106 (2025-06-30) was a settlement-service mTLS client certificate expiry with category credential_expiry and note 'no renewal automation'.

The error is on the client side: the rejected certificate is our own payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (alert 45, remote error), i.e., payment-service presented an expired client cert to the bank.

refs.quote: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal

findings.statement: The green HTTP error_rate is a false negative because failed bank transactions are marked PENDING_RETRY (async/retryable) rather than returning HTTP 5xx, so the 5xx-based panel misses them.
